newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mixed on selling in electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mixed on selling in electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed virtually unchanged on Monday as early gains were erased by profit-taking in the electronic sector, brokers said.
The weighted index ended just 0.97 points or 0.01 percent higher at 6,626.41. Turnover was a hectic T$71.66 billion.
The electronics sector lost 0.92 percent as profit-takers cashed in on recent gains spurred by September's year-high in the U.S. semiconductor industry's book-to-bill ratio.
"No sector has been able to sustain a rise, so investors figured it was time to switch holdings," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
Both Primax Electronics and D-Link Corp plunged the daily seven percent limit, or T$4.50 and T$3.50 respectively, to T$64.50 and T$51. Acer Peripherals dropped 5.94 percent or T$3 to T$47.50.
Some investors switched their buying focus to recently slumping food shares, lifting the sector by 0.53 percent.
"The various sectors are basically alternating between bargain-hunting and profit-taking because the overall market lacks a clear direction," Hou said.
Brokers noted a strong technical resistance at 6,680.66, the year-high level established on October 5.
"The index will stay pretty flat for a while unless a major new factor appears to upset the balance of trade," said Lin Long-hsien of Unitd Securities.
A 6,590-6,660 range was seen for Tuesday.
